correctness.rationale: Reconstructed common-root identity D_i=e2+x_i e1+x_i^2 and derivative difference (x_i+x_j)sum_{l neq i,j}x_l; these hold over an algebraic closure, force at most two coordinate values, then characteristic-two block parity yields only support-size 1 mod4. Localization at each point inverts cross-block differences, proving all same-block coordinates scheme-theoretically identical. The resulting chart ring is k when n odd and k[b]/(b^2) for 4|n; the exceptional single-block point is covered by the nondegenerate projective derivative matrix. The quadratic tangent polar form is nondegenerate for odd n, and for even n its one-dimensional radical has nonzero quadratic value, so the projective quadric is smooth. Euler 3F=sum xi Di makes the gradient scheme the singular scheme in char2. Roots-of-unity filtration gives the count. Independently exhausted all projective GF(2) points for n=3,4,5,7,8,9,11 and GF(4) points for n=3,4,5,7,8; matched 3,4,6,28,64,136,528 and no extra GF4 points. Finite field tests corroborate, not establish, the algebraic-closure theorem.
